races.name: Navan Racecourse Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Supreme Lord
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a solid course profile — three runs on Good ground, all producing placed finishes, and the step back to 6f after an 8f outing suits; Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is a positive for a horse that stays on rather than quickens.|

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground on debut and is redistributed to the lead as the only confirmed pace-setter; races out of its natural hold-up role, so its STYLE_FIT score of 0.80 tempers expectations, but the controlled gallop it creates is entirely self-authored and the Going to Firm surface is a proven strength across four runs.|

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: Unknown style with three runs all on Good ground showing mid-division finishes, and the unresolved profile means Jack Kearney's tactical call in the first furlong will define where this horse ends up; placed on a 6f course trip last time suggests the distance is no concern.|

runners_data.name: Prince Of Peppard
runners_data.note: Struggling for form with three consecutive double-figure finishes, and while Ben Coen is a significant booking, this horse's natural instinct to race last leaves it needing a troubled pace to create late openings — squeezed further up the track as one of several genuine closers mapped to midfield.|

runners_data.name: Two Brigade
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on a horse that has been tried in headgear (blinkers) and is still searching for form after four runs without a placing; its true preference is to finish from the rear, but the crowded hold-up division means it cannot easily adopt that position, reducing its chance to land a telling blow.|

runners_data.name: Lucy's Promise
runners_data.note: Flagged for a fade-in-finish tendency across five Good-ground runs with no placing, and with the shortest preparation of the field at just seven days since its last outing, a repeat of those late-race struggles is the primary concern; sits in midfield on the map but will want to come from further back.|

runners_data.name: No Time Faults
runners_data.note: Wearing a hood and returning after 22 days off, this horse has finished last or second-last in three of four starts and is marked as a fader — a true rear-of-field runner mapped to midfield by necessity rather than preference, and the Good to Firm surface has not unlocked anything positive across its entire career.|

runners_data.name: Little Diva
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) applied, three runs all on Good ground with finishes of 10th, 9th and 5th at shorter 5f, and the switch up to 6f is an open question; one of several hold-up horses placed higher on the map than natural instinct dictates, and Wesley Joyce's claim may help it get a better pitch, but the fade pattern is a recurring concern.|

races.paceDynamic: Howlin Wolf is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 6f nursery handicap on Good to Firm ground at Navan, and with no genuine rival to press from the outside, the pace will be controlled and sustainable rather than frantic — a tempo that keeps the race honest without stringing the field out. The remaining seven runners are all hold-up types by nature, with Prince Of Peppard, Two Brigade, Lucy's Promise, No Time Faults and Little Diva redistributed into midfield slots purely because the race map cannot accommodate them all at the rear; their true preference is to race last and finish late. Someday Somewhere's style is unspecified but recent 6f placings suggest a prominent lean, while Supreme Lord is a genuine hold-up operator with course-and-distance form on similar going. This field carries far more hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear — Prince Of Peppard, Two Brigade, Lucy's Promise, No Time Faults and Little Diva are all true closers who will compete for the same late ground, and the most likely beneficiary of a controlled, single-paced gallop is a horse that can track midfield and produce one sustained run, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the one to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Howlin Wolf Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Howlin Wolf sets a measured, uncontested lead and the field settles without drama, turning sustained stamina into an advantage.
scenarios.body: Howlin Wolf dictates a comfortable gallop, burns off rivals in the final furlong before the closers can organise, and the Good to Firm surface rewards a horse that handles it well — four out of four in similar conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Howlin Wolf's pace is just genuine enough to stretch the closers wide, allowing one sharp midfield tracker to thread through and collar the leader.
scenarios.body: A horse racing in the first half of the field picks up the tempo at the two-furlong pole and runs through beaten rivals as the early leader flattens out on the Good to Firm surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than it looks and the field concertinas in the final furlong, opening a gap for true hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: With the majority of the field sharing the same late-running instinct, one or two closers can cut through if the early gallop takes a toll on Howlin Wolf; however the sheer number of hold-up types competing for the same ground limits how likely a clean passage is.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems among the dense pocket of hold-up horses cause interference in the straight, resulting in a chaotic finish where a fresh-legged runner benefits from a clear run.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of five hold-up types into the middle of the field creates a genuinely congested mid-race pack, and in a messy finish a horse with a wide draw or an early decision to switch lanes by an experienced jockey could profit.

watchPoints.text: Howlin Wolf is the pace engine here — if it struggles to stride out naturally from an unfamiliar front-running position, the gallop could be falsely steady and render the entire field a blanket finish.|

The cluster of five hold-up types (Prince Of Peppard, Two Brigade, Lucy's Promise, No Time Faults, Little Diva) will all be seeking the same racing room in the straight — watch for traffic interference around the two-furlong marker that could cost any one of them a winning run.|

Supreme Lord has the strongest case for a clean passage from an organised midfield position and has posted placed finishes in all three Good-ground starts — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle positions aggressively early to avoid the hold-up traffic.|

Good to Firm conditions at Navan reward horses with a clean action and previous form on similar ground — Howlin Wolf (4/4), Supreme Lord (3/3) and Someday Somewhere (3/3) all have unblemished records on this surface, giving them a meaningful edge over horses without that confirmation.|

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Colin Keane and G M Lyons, who drops back from a recent run over 6f on Good ground where she finished fifth; her two wins in similar conditions suggest she handles this going well, and Keane's ability to thread through in big-field sprints is her best asset here.|

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Sam Coen (5) takes the ride for Denis Hogan on this four-year-old who has winning form over 6f on Good ground and has run into the frame at this trip recently; his natural prominent style suits a race with a contested lead, and he is one of the more likely horses to secure that position just off Cool Azul's shoulder.|

runners_data.name: Back Down Under
runners_data.note: Reese Holohan (7) takes over on this five-year-old for Padraig Roche, who carries a tongue tie and has consistent 6f form on Good ground across 15 runs; returning from 40 days off is a mild query, but his prominent style at this trip fits the race shape well and he should be prominent throughout.|

runners_data.name: Cool Azul
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this three-year-old for A Oliver, a confirmed front-runner who most recently won over this 6f course and distance 9 days ago on Good ground; the key question is whether Smoke Them Out will force him into a contested lead that costs him in the closing stages, which is a real risk in a field of 14.|

runners_data.name: By The Lake
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount for Derek McCormack on this lightly-raced three-year-old returning from 321 days off, having won over 5f on Good to Firm at Navan previously; the long absence is a significant concern, and hold-up tactics from a wide draw in a big sprint field after that layoff make this a speculative proposition.|

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge rides for H Rogers on a six-year-old who has won twice over 6f on Good ground recently and wears a hood; this horse's natural instinct is to race from off the pace, but in a 14-runner sprint it is unlikely to find its ideal position at the rear, which is a material consideration when assessing its chances.|

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this veteran eight-year-old for Edward Lynam, last seen winning over 6f on Good ground 81 days ago and fitted with a tongue tie; his true running style is from hold-up position, and the crowded nature of this sprint field makes it hard for him to get back far enough to produce his characteristic late run.|

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Terry Casey (7) takes the ride for Daniel James Murphy on this progressive three-year-old who won over 5f on Good ground 18 days ago; rated OR 78 and wearing a tongue tie, she races from hold-up position but has the fitness and recent winning form to be dangerous if she finds clear running in the closing stages.|

runners_data.name: Sporting Hero
runners_data.note: Jamie Orr (7) rides for William Durkan on a six-year-old who has been in very poor recent form over sprint trips, including consecutive zeros; his win came over 5f on Good ground but the 7-day turnaround and blinkered hold-up tactics in a competitive 14-runner field makes his prospects of reversing that slide limited.|

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: Sadhbh Tormey (7) partners this four-year-old for T G McCourt, a confirmed front-runner whose best form has come over 5-7f but who has not won in recent outings; her role here is to contest the early lead with Cool Azul, and if she does not fold quickly she will dictate how hard the pace is run — her stamina at 6f on fast ground is unproven.|

runners_data.name: Tornado Kiss
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and jockeys this three-year-old, who was off 85 days before this run and has won over 5f on Good ground; a prominent runner returning from a break, the combination of the step up in trip from recent outings and the layoff introduces some uncertainty, but the trainer-jockey combination keeps things simple.|

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman (7) rides for Eddie & Patrick Harty on a five-year-old with two recent wins over 5f on Good ground; this mare's instinct is to race from the back of the field, but forced into a mid-race position in a competitive 14-runner sprint, her ability to produce a meaningful late effort from further off the pace than she prefers is the central uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: All The Girls
runners_data.note: James Ryan rides for T G McCourt on this three-year-old who wears a tongue tie and has struggled to convert minor form into wins over 6f; her best efforts have come when racing prominently, but she has no wins to her name on Good ground over this trip and her chance hinges on a strong pace to close into.|

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Adam Caffrey rides this seven-year-old for Adrian McGuinness, who boasts the most active 14-day record in the field; fitted with a visor, this veteran's form has been confined to 7f lately, the step down to 6f on fast ground is a query, and its natural hold-up style will be difficult to execute in a pressed 14-runner sprint field.|

races.paceDynamic: Cool Azul and Smoke Them Out are the two confirmed front-runners in this 14-runner 6f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Navan, and with both likely to press hard from the gates, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the off — neither is a natural lone leader who can dictate at their own tempo. The battle between Cool Azul and Smoke Them Out through the first two furlongs will set an honest sectional that compresses the field and keeps the race true, giving prominent racers who can latch onto the pace without burning energy a genuine platform to challenge. Several horses tagged as redistributed — Jon Riggens, Gotta Catch'em All, Mary Shoelaces, and Flaming Rib — are genuine hold-up types who will struggle to get all the way to the rear in a 14-runner sprint field running at this tempo, and of the prominent types, Alfred Tennyson, Back Down Under, and Tornado Kiss are most likely to actually secure that position just off the speed. This contested pace shape on fast ground over 6f at a flat track like Navan classically favours horses who can race prominently in the slipstream of the pace-setters and produce a sustained late kick — the prominent-to-midfield profile, travelling into the race rather than making it, is the one to be on here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Cool Azul and Smoke Them Out fight for the lead and set a genuine gallop that stretches the field from the outset.
scenarios.body: The honest early fractions burn off the pure front-runners approaching the final two furlongs, leaving the race to those who tracked the pace economically and hit the line with something in reserve; on Good to Firm ground at Navan's flat 6f, prominent types who switch off behind the speed have the cleanest route to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Cool Azul breaks cleanly and secures a comfortable lead while Smoke Them Out settles for second-fiddle role without a prolonged duel.
scenarios.body: With the pace pressure reduced to a manageable level, Cool Azul can control the fractions, quicken at the two-furlong pole, and simply outrun the field on its most recent winning form over this exact course and distance; prominent types just off the pace still get first run but face a leader who has not been harried.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flyer Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely detonates early and the field spreads wide, creating a gap for the handful of genuine closers to motor through late.
scenarios.body: Amiata and Sovereign Cry, the most credible true hold-up horses here with course-and-distance form on similar going, are the most likely beneficiaries if they can find a clear passage in a 14-runner field; the risk is that the redistribution of so many hold-up horses into midfield means the real deep-closers are blocked in a congested final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surges
scenarios.trigger: If Smoke Them Out over-races in the early stages and pulls Cool Azul faster than intended, causing both to stop sharply inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A strong midfield surge materialises as the leaders capitulate, and the horses who were neither fighting for the lead nor trailing from the back find themselves in the ideal position; this remains the least likely shape given both front-runners have recent form suggesting they handle honest gallops without stopping.

watchPoints.text: Cool Azul and Smoke Them Out will be fighting for the lead from the off — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which, if either, blinks and settles, as this will determine whether the pace is truly hot or merely honest.

By The Lake's 321-day absence is extreme for a three-year-old in a competitive sprint handicap — Dylan Browne McMonagle's presence keeps it interesting, but watch for any signs of rustiness in the paddock and early stages.

Jon Riggens and Gotta Catch'em All are both natural hold-up horses who are highly unlikely to get to the rear of a 14-runner sprint with genuine pace — watch whether they end up trapped in mid-division with nowhere to go in the final furlong.

Alfred Tennyson's recent step down from 7f to 6f should be monitored from the gates — if Sam Coen can get him settled just off the speed rather than chasing the pace, he is the horse most likely to be travelling best at the two-furlong marker.

Amiata has been busy recently and Colin Keane will be looking for a gap to appear in the final furlong — in a 14-runner sprint this is not guaranteed, and any signs of traffic trouble early in the straight will be telling for her chance of running on.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Abletai
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with four runs on similar good ground and consistent placed form at 5f, trainer Grassick in modest recent form (1 from 6 in 14 days) but this horse handles the conditions and will travel handily just off the lead — 39 days since last run is the main query.

runners_data.name: Always Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping back from 7f to 5f, which is a significant drop in trip and creates a real doubt about whether she can get competitive in time on a flat straight; going is fine (2 from 2 on similar), but the style-trip combination is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Atlantic Bridge
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only two starts, both returning 4th on good ground, and style is unclassified — Dylan Browne McMonagle is a major positive, but no win or place from either run raises questions about genuine ability even if the booking signals stable confidence; trip looks fine.

runners_data.name: Better Yet
runners_data.note: Just one run to her name — a 3rd at 5f on good — and is an obvious place contender if that form translates; Shane Foley retains the ride and Mrs Harrington's stable (2 from 31 in 14 days) is not in a purple patch, but Better Yet's prominent style makes her naturally suited to an uncontested pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Jungle Tina
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant with no public form to assess, going preference unknown; Jarlath Fahey has had zero returns from three runners in the past fortnight, but debut unknowns always carry a wildcard element that cannot be dismissed in an open maiden.

runners_data.name: Rathbran Lady
runners_data.note: Form figures of 10 and 12 across her two starts tell a bleak story, and she is tagged as a finisher who fades — a hold-up style on a flat 5f track against more experienced horses makes this a very difficult task; trainer Mulvany's recent form (1 from 14) does little to encourage.

runners_data.name: Rollin'onariver
runners_data.note: Another unraced debutant with no public data available; Chris Hayes is a capable jockey who can place a debutant favourably, and Denis Hogan's string has had two winners from 24 in the last fortnight — a stable capable of producing a ready first-time runner on the right day.

runners_data.name: Southern Boulevard
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the key pace setter — three runs at this exact trip on similar ground and two places suggest he handles conditions, and with Colin Keane in the saddle and G M Lyons (3 from 24 in 14 days) behind him, he is not just a pace facilitator; the question is whether he can sustain the lead over 5f without being pressured.

runners_data.name: Syrah
runners_data.note: Finished 14th on debut at 5f on good ground and is tagged as fading in the finish — a hold-up style that showed no finishing acceleration first time out, and Patrick McGettigan (5lb claim) is a minor upside; Charles Weld has had zero winners from four recent runners and the overall picture is hard to construct positively.

races.paceDynamic: Southern Boulevard is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 5f maiden and, with no other horse in the field sharing that lead profile, Colin Keane can dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the gates. The pace is therefore likely to be sustainable rather than scorching — Southern Boulevard has placed twice from three starts at this trip on similar ground and will not be under pressure to burn early, meaning the fractions should be honest but manageable. Abletai and Better Yet will push up into prominent positions just behind, giving a small group of handy types a short run through with the hold-up horses — Always Magic, Rathbran Lady, and Syrah — needing to produce sustained late runs on a flat track that offers no topography to help compress the race. On a flat course with a controlled lead and no pace battle, prominent runners sitting just off the front rank are best placed: they travel economically, avoid traffic, and have minimal ground to close, while true closers face the prospect of a winner gone clear before the final furlong with no pace injection to assist them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Follows
scenarios.trigger: If Southern Boulevard dictates an uncontested lead and the prominent chasers track efficiently to challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Southern Boulevard sets a metronomic pace that flatters the prominent types camped just behind, with Abletai and Better Yet ideally positioned to pounce without needing a finishing kick they may not possess; the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up when the leader has not burned early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Override
scenarios.trigger: If Better Yet or Abletai press Southern Boulevard hard from the break, lifting the tempo and setting up a closer's finish.
scenarios.body: A quicker early fractions would see the lead pack tire inside the final 100 yards, giving a well-timed hold-up run a genuine chance of catching a tiring leader; Always Magic, who has shown decent form in a small sample, would be the primary beneficiary from the back of the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced runners — Jungle Tina or Rollin'onariver — has been prepared for an immediate forward show and bolts up on debut.
scenarios.body: With unknown quantities holding style tags as unclassified, either debutant could have been schooled aggressively and produce a one-run performance that catches the field cold; trainers Denis Gerard Hogan and Jarlath P Fahey both have the stable form to spring a debut surprise in a soft maiden.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Southern Boulevard fades dramatically in the final furlong and the entire prominent group flattens out, handing the race to a late finisher.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires several things to go wrong simultaneously — the leader collapsing, the prominent horses running flat — and the hold-up runners in this field (Rathbran Lady, Syrah) have shown little evidence of the finishing punch needed; Rathbran Lady has recorded finishing positions of 10 and 12, making this scenario the least likely of the four.

watchPoints.text: Southern Boulevard — if Colin Keane is able to dictate the pace completely uncontested through the first two furlongs, the race shape crystallises immediately around him and the prominent pair tracking him become the danger horses rather than closers.

Jungle Tina and Rollin'onariver — both debut runners with zero public form; either could have been laid out for this race and produce an unexpectedly forward display that distorts the shape entirely, especially if one breaks fast and takes the race by the scruff.

Better Yet — only one run in the book, but it was a solid 3rd at this exact trip and going; if she travels smoothly into the race in the prominent position, she is the most unexposed horse with a realistic credentials to challenge Southern Boulevard.

Always Magic — the drop from 7f to 5f for a hold-up horse is a pattern worth tracking in-running; if she is still last or second-last at halfway, she is almost certainly out of the race given the flat straight offers no late compression of the field.

Atlantic Bridge — the Dylan Browne McMonagle booking on a lightly raced, unclassified filly is the market watch point; if she opens with any confidence in the market, it suggests the stable knows more than the form figures of two 4th-place finishes imply.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Optional Claiming Maiden

runners_data.name: Equus Victor
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the mount for Daniel Murphy on this confirmed front-runner who has form over 5f and 8f; an uncontested lead on Good to Firm Navan is a significant gift and his 12-day turnaround looks sharp.|

runners_data.name: Jezzie Bea
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides for Mrs Harrington; went four times in similar going (2/2 sim-going) at 7f and 8f, both placed fourth, suggesting she handles conditions but lacks a finishing kick — her style is unclassified so she may be capable of tracking the pace and challenging.|

runners_data.name: Leadlight
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien sends out this Dylan Browne McMonagle-ridden runner who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature; the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the crowded rear, not his preferred racing position, and his style-fit discount (0.90) is warranted — he ran 4th and 6th in similar going.|

runners_data.name: This That
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount for G M Lyons carries a fade warning in the finish and has placed eighth, ninth, and fourth in three similar-going starts; a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield only by necessity, and his tendency to weaken late on Good ground is a meaningful concern over this trip.|

runners_data.name: Summer Sent You
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this K J Condon runner returning seven days after a 12th-place finish; two starts, both on Good going over 7f, produced 10th and 12th — the fade warning is fully supported by the form and the step up to a mile looks unlikely to reverse the trend.|

runners_data.name: Ferronniere
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes debuts for Denis Hogan on unknown going; no form data, no days-since-last-run figure, and going tolerance is unestablished — an unknown quantity that must be respected on class grounds alone but carries the standard debutante risk in an 0-race profile.|

runners_data.name: Mickian Thomas
runners_data.note: Luke McAteer rides for Rory Devine; sole start produced a 16th-place finish over 6f on Good going and the fade-in-finish flag is already attached after one run — nothing in the profile suggests the step to a mile will be an improvement.|

races.paceDynamic: Equus Victor is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival capable or likely to dispute the lead, he can dictate terms from the front at whatever tempo suits Daniel James Murphy's stable. Good to Firm conditions at Navan over a flat mile will suit a horse that can control fractions, and an uncontested lead at this pace is a significant tactical advantage. The redistribution note is important here: Leadlight and This That are genuine hold-up horses shuffled into a midfield map position simply because the visual rear is overcrowded — in practice, the true rearward cluster of Summer Sent You, Mickian Thomas, Leadlight, and This That will likely fill the back half of this field, leaving Equus Victor freer still. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or close-tracking prominent horse who can exploit the uncontested lead and hold on through the final two furlongs on quick ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Equus Victor Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Equus Victor leads uncontested and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that denies the closers a target.
scenarios.body: Equus Victor dictates every yard, his rivals burn energy chasing from the back on fast ground, and he quickens clear entering the final furlong before they can close. Horses with pace or prominent early positions are the primary beneficiaries as the leader's rhythm converts into a winning margin.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Equus Victor sets a genuinely strong pace that leaves him vulnerable, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A runner like Jezzie Bea or Ferronniere, positioned just off the pace and travelling comfortably, gets a clean run to challenge as Equus Victor's stamina is tested by the quick ground. The even, flat mile suits a horse that can switch off in second or third before producing a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Comes Good
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the straight, creating a genuine sprint finish that allows the back markers to close.
scenarios.body: A runner like Leadlight, who is a genuine hold-up type despite being mapped to midfield due to redistribution, finds the gap in a bunched finish and produces a late thrust. This scenario is tempered by the redistribution: the supposed closers are not truly positioned to exploit it, and fast ground further reduces their margin for error.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From Maiden Debutante
scenarios.trigger: If Ferronniere, making her racecourse debut, is significantly ahead of her mark and produces an unexposed performance that outclasses the field.
scenarios.body: Ferronniere's going profile is unknown and she is lightly raced, but a debut win for the Denis Hogan yard is possible if the training gallops have produced a ready-made performer. This scenario requires her to overcome the standard maiden debut disadvantage and a field that contains at least one horse with proven course-going form.

watchPoints.text: Equus Victor must be monitored at the break — if he misses the start or is crowded off the rail, he loses his key tactical advantage and the entire race shape collapses around him.

Leadlight and This That are genuine hold-up horses who will be looking for cover that may not exist if the pace is slow; watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle attempts to push Leadlight forward against his natural style, which could compromise both his run and the finishing positions of those behind him.

Summer Sent You and Mickian Thomas both carry fade warnings and have shown a consistent inability to sustain effort in the closing stages — if either is still in contention entering the final two furlongs, it could signal a falsely run race that distorts the result.

Ferronniere's debut on unknown going is the principal wildcard; watch her paddock behaviour and early positioning — if Chris Hayes sends her prominent rather than settling mid-pack, she could be better than her unknown profile suggests.

races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle This Saturday Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Bill Silvers
runners_data.note: Held-up profile with visor, showing poor recent form (P and 0s), last run 15 days ago; similar-going record over this trip is modest (0 wins, 0 places) and the apprentice booking offers no meaningful claim advantage in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with decent recent course experience over 8f on Good, a win and two places on similar ground across 15 runs suggests genuine aptitude; Sam Coen's 5lb claim is useful but this horse rarely fires in big fields.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Three wins from last five starts, all at 8f on Good going, wearing a tongue-tie — the form profile is outstanding for this race shape; Patrick McGettigan's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable and the recent Navan form reads well on this surface.

runners_data.name: In A Hurry
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, clear leader in race-shape terms; 57 days off the track is a query but this is Good to Firm which suits, and Keith Henry Clarke sends runners back fit — the tactical advantage of uncontested lead is significant in a compressed field.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood, two wins on Good going at 7-8f, and Dylan Browne McMonagle booked for a typically prominent ride; trainer has no runners in the 14-day window suggesting this is a targeted run, and the style fits Scenario A precisely.

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true style is to come from the rear, but the volume of hold-up types forces him into a midfield position where he is racing out of role; Gavin Cromwell's consistent yard and an 11-day turnaround suggest freshness, yet the style compromise tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a patchy recent record at 8f on Good — three runs at this distance returned only one minor placing; Terry Casey's 7lb claim helps but form figures suggest this horse has lost its way rather than found a competitive opportunity.

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as a fader in the finish, with a concerning record (0 wins, 0 places on Good going across his limited sample); young 3yo up against older, more experienced handicappers — the fade flag makes him very hard to back in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form has deteriorated significantly (two 0s and three double-figure positions at this trip), and the stable has no recent winners in the 14-day window; nothing in the data suggests a bounce-back here.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with Colin Keane aboard — a significant jockey booking — but displaced into midfield by the congested hold-up division; his two placed efforts at 8f on Good are noted, and Keane's ability to manufacture a run adds a wild card despite the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a genuine hold-up specialist pushed forward in the map due to redistribution; has a win at 10f and places at 8-9f on Good going, suggesting stamina is not an issue, though racing out of preferred role blunts his typical finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old flagged as a finisher who fades, with a visor in the plate; hold-up horse displaced into midfield, modest recent form, and the fade flag in combination with the redistribution makes this one of the least compelling runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Interesting 3yo who won over 10f on Good going recently, now dropping back to a mile — the drop in trip may sharpen him; natural hold-up runner mapped to midfield, but Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim and a live recent form figure (1) make him more interesting than most in this group.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago — an exceptionally quick turnaround that raises significant fitness and recovery questions; wears a tongue-tie, fades in the finish, and has a string of double-figure finishes at this trip; the redistribution into midfield from the hold-up role makes the profile doubly awkward.

races.paceDynamic: In A Hurry is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and faces no credible challengers for the lead, meaning she can bowl along at a controlled, self-regulated tempo on Good to Firm ground at Navan over one mile — a recipe for a sustainable, uncontested gallop rather than a scorching pace. Gloriously Glam and Go Out will look to press from the front rank, but with In A Hurry setting the fractions unchallenged, the pace is unlikely to be severe enough to blow the field apart early. The large cluster of hold-up horses — Tofino, Kc Bear, Alto Sax, Nephin Mountain, Cordouan, and Lohengrin — cannot all find their natural position at the rear; several will be shuffled into midfield against their instinct, compressing the pack and making a truly strung-out, searingly-run contest unlikely. This race shape — a lone leader dictating a moderate-to-fair pace — strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can travel into contention without burning energy, particularly those with proven form on Good-to-Firm ground over this mile trip; deep closers will find the pace insufficient to generate the late gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If In A Hurry dictates a fair but uncontested tempo and the prominent/just-off-pace brigade track efficiently into the straight.
scenarios.body: In A Hurry sets an honest rhythm that rewards those travelling close to the pace, and horses like Gloriously Glam and Minaun View — both proven on this going and trip — are ideally placed to pounce entering the final two furlongs. Minaun View's recent sequence of wins at 8f on Good going makes her the textbook profile beneficiary; Gloriously Glam's prominent style and Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard add significant potency.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If In A Hurry's controlled solo lead is slow enough that no one commits to chasing and she steals the race from the front.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace that nobody is willing to pressurise means In A Hurry bowls into the straight with a clear advantage and enough reserves to hold on despite giving weight away, particularly if the chasing pack has burned energy jostling for position on the home turn. This is a genuine risk in a 14-runner handicap where the redistribution of hold-up horses into midfield creates a crowded, disorganised pursuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough — or a prominent runner overcooks it — to create late gaps for a finisher coming from deep.
scenarios.body: A horse like Kc Bear or Tofino, who would naturally want to come from off the pace, can capitalise if the race develops into a proper test — but the redistribution of multiple hold-up types into the midfield reduces their ability to produce a true sustained late run as they are already compromised positionally. Colin Keane on Kc Bear gives this outcome more plausibility than the others in this group, but the race shape must deviate significantly from the expected pattern for closers to truly land.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Compressed Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant traffic problems on the turn, scrambling race-positions and producing a muddling, unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: With 14 runners, several horses displaced from their preferred positions, and a single front-runner stretching no one, the home straight could become a lottery of gaps and interference rather than a clean test of form. Minaun View's consistency and Nephin Mountain's recent win at this course and distance give them resilience in a messy scenario, but form figures and pace profile become far less reliable guides.

watchPoints.text: Minaun View has three wins at exactly this trip and going combination in her last five runs — if she is given a clean prominent run by McGettigan she is the standout profile match for this race shape and any drifting in the market should be treated with suspicion.

In A Hurry has been off 57 days and is a 4yo returning without a recent prep run — watch the early market move carefully, as any significant drift could signal the handler doubts her readiness to deliver a front-running performance.

Lohengrin ran just 48 hours ago and is attempting to back-up on Good to Firm ground; monitor for any official vet scrutiny or late withdrawal, as a 2-day turnaround for a hold-up type with a fading flag is a serious welfare and form concern.

Colin Keane takes the ride on Kc Bear, representing the most notable jockey-trainer pairing (Noel Meade) in the field — Keane rarely accepts routine rides in handicaps and his presence on a hold-up horse displaced into midfield is worth tracking in running, as he will manufacture ground if a gap appears.

With six runners tagged as redistributed hold-up horses compressed into the midfield, watch the early stages closely for crowding on the first bend — a stumble or interference between Tofino, Nephin Mountain, Alto Sax and Cordouan could compromise multiple horses before the race has properly begun.

races.paceDynamic: Mythical Rock is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner handicap over a mile at Navan on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rivals pressing for the early lead, Sean Davis can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being harassed through the opening furlongs. Borora Aura is the only other horse with prominent inclinations and may track Mythical Rock closely, but the pace is unlikely to be genuinely searching, creating a race that could easily develop into a bunched, slowly-run affair in the early stages before a sprint-like finish off a modest tempo. The field is exceptionally hold-up heavy — Cosmic Funk, Ella's Gold, Sheamus Seimhiu, Think About It, Kingcharles, The Holy Apostle and Hale Bopp are all natural closers redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the field cannot accommodate that many true hold-up types at the rear simultaneously. This race shape heavily favours prominent racers and horses with a strong late turn of foot that can be delivered from a handy position, as a sustainable pace will compress the field late and make it very difficult for genuine deep closers to generate the momentum they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mythical Rock Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Mythical Rock is allowed to bowl along uncontested and the pace remains sustainable throughout the mile.
scenarios.body: Mythical Rock sets a metronomic gallop from the front on Going to Firm ground that suits, and with no rivals willing or able to challenge the lead, the field strings out in chase before a mid-race lull turns the race into a sprint finish from the home turn; horses racing prominently behind are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick From Handy Spot
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses enough midrace that horses settled just off the leaders in the first half-dozen stalls produce a sprint-finish burst from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A compressed field tracking Mythical Rock at a sustainable clip means horses like Loingseoir and Comfort Line, who have the form at this trip on Good ground, can produce a late surge without needing to cover excessive ground; the hold-up types pushed furthest back will struggle to reach them in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that the field bunches entirely and a wall of closers swarms the front in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace would theoretically allow the redistributed hold-up horses to get competitive, but because so many of them — Cosmic Funk, Ella's Gold, Think About It — are not truly racing in their natural role here, the finishing kick required to sprint from the pack may not materialise at the critical moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Caught Late
scenarios.trigger: If Borora Aura or another presser forces a stronger early pace that ultimately ties up Mythical Rock in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A contested pace would set up a genuine test of stamina over the mile, and any horse with a strong cruising speed and confirmed form at 1m on Good to Firm would pick up the pieces; however, this field lacks a horse clearly dominant enough in that profile to make this scenario reliable.

watchPoints.text: Mythical Rock is the race-shaper — if Sean Davis gets a clean break and the lead goes uncontested, the race is likely run entirely to this horse's strengths and no prominent rival may be able to close the gap in time.

Comfort Line and Loingseoir both have multiple recent places on Good going at 8f and arrive in form — if the pace is sustainable and the finish comes off the front, these two are the most dangerous late movers from off a handy position.

Sheamus Seimhiu's 304-day absence combined with the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and a style mismatch makes this a significant non-runner-style risk — connections should be monitored for any market drift that would indicate lack of preparation confidence.

Hale Bopp runs just two days after its last start — an unusually quick bounce for an eight-year-old that warrants caution; if the horse shows any signs of flat work in the market, discount accordingly.

Trumph's ⚠ fade-in-finish flag is worth monitoring through the race — if Shane Foley gets a prominent position in the first half-mile, watch whether the horse holds that position turning in or weakens, as that will be informative for future assessments at this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Sunrush and Mare Crisium are the two confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner field over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Navan, and both are likely to contest the lead from the break, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a soft, unchallenged pace. With two horses fighting for the front, the tempo should be honest throughout — this is not a race where either pace-setter can coast and conserve — which will stretch the field and expose any stamina limitations, particularly significant on Good to Firm ground at this trip. The redistribution note is important: Werifesteria, Strike De Vega, Cascade Canyon, Connecteo, Millhone, Soigne, Chapel Island, Chloe's Boy, Stabannon, Cameclose and Nando Lily are all natural hold-up horses pushed into a congested midfield map, but their true roles remain at the back; among the prominent types, Essential Comedy, Chicago Moon, Blissful Bonita and Love Orchid are the most likely to actually secure a forward position in running. This race shape — a contested, honest gallop over a stamina-testing trip in fast conditions — firmly favours hold-up horses with proven form at 1m4f-plus on good ground who possess genuine staying power, with prominent-racing types who can travel sweetly behind the pace and pick up in the straight also well-placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Sunrush and Mare Crisium fight for the lead and sustain a genuine gallop that stretches the field from halfway
scenarios.body: The honest pace set by two front-runners over 1m6f on Good to Firm will drain the leaders and reward horses with authentic stamina who travel smoothly in rear; hold-up horses with proven staying form at 12f-14f on good ground will be best positioned to pick off tiring rivals in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners cracks early, leaving a single pace-setter who sets only a moderate tempo that suits a prominent racer travelling behind
scenarios.body: A horse like Essential Comedy or Blissful Bonita who settles just off the pace avoids the attritional early battle and arrives at the turn with energy to burn; on Good to Firm, a prominent position becomes even more valuable as hold-up horses who have been compressed into midfield struggle to find room in a big field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners over-press each other and blow up turning for home, opening a gap for the deepest closers
scenarios.body: A genuine pace collapse in the final quarter-mile would theoretically suit the truest hold-up horses, but most are mapped to midfield due to redistribution and may not achieve their natural position; any late surge is therefore more likely to come from a horse like Love Orchid or Cascade Canyon who has the stamina and a clear passage than from those buried at the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of Sunrush or Mare Crisium destroys the other early, opens a clear lead and is allowed to bowl along at their own rhythm
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground over 1m6f a relaxed front-runner can be very hard to reel in if the pack allows a gap to develop; however with two confirmed pace-setters this scenario requires one to fold quickly, making it the least likely shape, and neither front-runner carries a form profile that strongly suggests they can dominate a field this large.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sunrush or Mare Crisium actually gets to the front unchallenged in the first furlong — if both press hard immediately, the race is on a very fast clock and stamina will be at a premium from the halfway point.

Chicago Moon wears blinkers and De Bromhead's yard is in excellent form; if W J Lee gets a prominent position just behind the front pair, watch him moving into contention turning for home as a potential improver who has already won at 12f on good ground.

Cascade Canyon's second-placed finish over 14f on good ground is the standout trip-and-going piece of form in this field — watch Dylan Browne McMonagle threading her through the big field in the straight even if she is held up further back than ideal.

With 18 runners and a large hold-up contingent compressed into midfield, watch for traffic problems in the home straight — horses drawn wide or with a clear passage are likely to have a meaningful positional advantage over those stuck on the rail in a bunched finish.

Millhone's three placed efforts at 11f-12f on good ground are the most consistent placed profile in the field; watch Rory Mulligan (5lb claim) — if she avoids the fade that has plagued her previously, she may run into a place at a competitive price.

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map due to the field's density of closers — the redistribution note (STYLE_FIT 0.90) is a meaningful discount, and a record of zero wins and zero places from 10 similar-going runs offers little encouragement regardless of where he settles.

runners_data.name: Macinamillion
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist shown in midfield purely by redistribution pressure; has two wins and four places from 12 good-ground runs with wins at 18f and 20f, so this 14f trip is shorter than ideal, and the STYLE_FIT (0.91) signals he is unlikely to reproduce his best from a non-natural position.

runners_data.name: Deluca Chop
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has won twice recently (13f soft, 13f good) and placed at 12f; Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim is useful and the visor headgear channels his energy — his recent in-form profile makes him one of the most interesting on-pace runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding wearing a pacemaker, displaced to midfield in the map; three places from 10 good-ground runs show some consistency but zero wins and a record predominantly at 14f to 18f means this 14f cut is not a major stretch, yet the redistribution limits his chance of producing his best.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare fitted with a visor, shown in midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.92); two placed efforts over 12f on good ground show she can be competitive but she has not won on this surface and will need a truly run race to get involved from her likely deep position.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: 4-year-old hold-up filly pushed into the midfield band; no wins or places on good ground from eight attempts, and a 12th last time at 14f — the redistribution compounds an already thin profile.

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fade flag, mapped to midfield due to redistribution; zero wins or places from six similar-going runs and a history of finishing in the teens on good ground — hard to find a scenario where she features.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: 4-year-old hold-up gelding shown in midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.93); fifth at 16f on good ground most recently which shows some stamina but zero wins or places on this surface from five runs limits expectation, even with Declan McDonogh taking the ride.

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: Prominent type who was 2nd at 12f on good ground three runs ago and has been placed at 16f — the trip and going are well within his range; Jared Huggan's 10lb claim is a significant weight pull and this is a sneaky on-pace candidate in a big field.

runners_data.name: Miners Cabin
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding with a pacemaker and a fade flag, redistributed to midfield; finishes in the 7th-to-15th range across nine recent good-ground runs and no win or place among them — consistently out of the frame.

runners_data.name: Share The Treasure
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare redistributed to midfield; 116 days off the track is a significant absence flag, and her best form came on soft/heavy ground (one win on soft) — the fast conditions here look against her.

runners_data.name: Phidias Ovation
runners_data.note: Likely hold-up type with a fade tendency, shown in midfield by redistribution; no jockey listed which itself is a red flag in a 26-runner field, and the recent form (10th, 16th, 7th, 12th) at shorter distances gives no confidence at 14f on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Lariat

races.paceDynamic: Makaiah is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 26-runner field, is set to roll along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Navan. Stepdance, Arcland, Deluca Chop, Highway Sixty One, and Jazz Forever are the prominent types who will press forward and fill positions just behind, creating a modestly-strung-out early shape rather than a true pace collapse. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Macinamillion, Eastern Blue Bird, Without Love, Maxwell Smart, and others have been redistributed from their natural rearward position into the midfield map because there are more genuine closers than the race shape can accommodate at the back; those most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace are Stepdance and Arcland, who have course-distance profile and trainer form behind them. A single uncontested front-runner setting a steady, even tempo over a flat 1m6f trip on fast ground is a textbook setup for prominent, on-pace runners who can track the leader, quicken from a handy position, and exploit rivals who get shuffled back in the traffic of a 26-strong field — the tactical verdict firmly favours the prominent style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Makaiah Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Makaiah bowls along uncontested and the pace is steady enough that tracking prominent horses arrive with a full tank.
scenarios.body: Makaiah's uncontested lead on good-to-firm ground sets a rhythmic tempo that suits horses travelling just behind — Stepdance and Arcland, both proven at this trip and going, can slot in behind and pounce in the straight without ever having to make up ground from deep. The flat Navan track and fast surface mean no premium on a late surge, directly favouring those who save energy by sitting on pace rather than chasing it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Makaiah goes too steady and the race turns into a late sprint, giving genuine closers a rare chance to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early tempo compresses the field approaching the home turn, and the dash to the line becomes a test of raw speed over the final two furlongs — on good-to-firm ground that rewards horses with residual freshness. Ms Messi and Anightaway both have recent wins at this trip on similar going and carry the tactical profile to benefit if a sprint-finish scenario plays out, though the crowded field complicates clean runs from deep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Makaiah Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely slow and Makaiah builds an insurmountable lead in a race where nothing commits to chasing early.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to go after a front-runner trotting along in a 26-runner handicap, Makaiah could coast into the straight with a two-length buffer that is never closed down on a flat track that offers no hiding place for chasers. The sim-going record (12/15 on similar ground) and the fact Shane Foley takes the ride underline a live each-way chance if the slow-pace scenario crystallises rather than being swept up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Big Field Produces Traffic Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the 26-runner field creates gridlock on the turn, shuffling back the hold-up horses and benefiting whichever handy type escapes cleanest.
scenarios.body: In a race of this size, horses at the rear face a near-impossible task threading through — redistributed closers like Macinamillion and Eastern Blue Bird, however talented on their best days, are denied their natural position and are most likely to get boxed in. The beneficiaries are the horses who have the tactical awareness and jockeys to find a clean path — Deluca Chop with Paddy Harnett aboard and Kevin The Great (Gary Carroll) have the profile to sneak through on a rail if gaps appear.
